name: Hornbill Festival
description: The world-renowned 'Festival of Festivals' celebrating all 16 major Naga tribes in their authentic architectural morungs.
cultural_significance: Spectacular tribal unity, warrior songs, folk dances, indigenous wrestling, traditional fire-making, Naga chilli eating contest, and nightly rock concerts.
visitor_tips: Book accommodation in Kisama or Kohima 3-4 months ahead. Tents and home-stays fill completely. Carry warm thermals as evening temperatures dip below 5°C.

name: Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu)
description: The heart and soul of Assamese culture, celebrating the arrival of spring, seeding season, and Assamese New Year.
cultural_significance: Graceful Bihu dance accompanied by Pepa (buffalo horn flute), Dhol, and Toka. Community feasts of Jolpan, Pitha, and Laroo.
visitor_tips: Visit open-air Bihu Sanmilans in Guwahati (Latasil, Judges Field). Taste authentic pitha from local village stalls. Friendly festive atmosphere everywhere.

name: Ziro Festival of Music
description: India's iconic eco-friendly outdoor indie music festival set against the pine-clad hills of the Apatani valley.
cultural_significance: Two solar-powered bamboo stages ('Donyi' and 'Polo') hosting independent artists from India and worldwide, surrounded by golden paddy fields.
visitor_tips: Camp in festival tents or book Hong village Apatani homestays early. Arunachal ILP is mandatory. Strictly single-use-plastic-free policy.

name: Manipur Sangai Festival
description: Named after the rare, dancing brow-antlered Sangai deer found only in Keibul Lamjao National Park on Loktak Lake.
cultural_significance: Mesmerizing classical Manipuri Raas Leela dance, indigenous Sagol Kangjei (ancestral polo), Thang-Ta martial arts, boat races, and hill-tribe handicrafts.
visitor_tips: Combine with canoe rides at Loktak Lake. Evenings in Imphal are lively with night food markets serving Singju and Eromba.

name: Chapchar Kut Spring Festival
description: The grandest, most colorful Mizo spring festival celebrated with immense enthusiasm after the completion of bamboo jhum clearing.
cultural_significance: Iconic Cheraw bamboo dance where agile performers step between clapping bamboo poles, traditional Vakiria feather headdresses, and community singing.
visitor_tips: Arrive at the Lammual ground by 9:30 AM for good viewing seats. Modest dress recommended. Taste festive Mizo Bai and smoked pork.

name: Wangala 100 Drums Festival
description: The signature harvest thanksgiving festival of the Garo tribe dedicated to the sun-god Misi Saljong.
cultural_significance: 100 master drummers beating long cylindrical drums (Dama) in hypnotic synchronization, accompanied by buffalo horn flutes and energetic line dancing.
visitor_tips: Stay in Tura town or village eco-camps. Try Garo festive rice beer (Chu) and spicy bamboo shoot chicken (Wak Gominda).

name: Torgya & Losar Monastic Festival
description: Ancient Monpa Buddhist festival to drive out evil spirits and welcome peace and prosperity in the new year.
cultural_significance: Lamas clad in intricate silk robes and ornate animal masks perform sacred monastic Cham dances in the snow-dusted monastery courtyard.
visitor_tips: Dress in heavy sub-zero woolens. Sela Pass may have snow; check road status. Photography of Cham dances is welcomed respectfully.

name: Kharchi Puja (Fourteen Deities Festival)
description: Centuries-old royal and tribal festival worshiping the 14 patron deities of Tripura to cleanse the Earth and Mother Nature.
cultural_significance: Immersion of royal deity idols in the sacred Howrah river, royal brass drums, tribal dances, and enormous seven-day cultural mela.
visitor_tips: Just 20 minutes by auto from Agartala city center. Open to all visitors. Great street food stalls featuring Tripuri bamboo snacks.

name: Pang Lhabsol Kanchenjunga Festival
description: Unique festival honoring Mount Kanchenjunga as the supreme protective guardian deity of Sikkim.
cultural_significance: Spectacular warrior dances (Dzonga dance) with dancers wielding swords and shields, dramatizing the historic brotherhood oath between Lepchas and Bhutias.
visitor_tips: Takes place in Gangtok palace monastery. Clear mountain mornings provide majestic glimpses of Kanchenjunga.

name: Majuli Raas Mahotsav
description: 500-year-old neo-Vaishnavite theatrical spectacle depicting Lord Krishna's divine life, enacted by thousands of islanders.
cultural_significance: Traditional handmade river-clay masks (Mukha) of demons and gods, classical Sattriya music, and all-night village plays across dozens of village stages.
visitor_tips: Ferries from Nimati Ghat run special night services. Book Majuli homestays well in advance; island atmosphere is electric.

name: Nongkrem Royal Dance Festival
description: Sacred thanksgiving harvest ritual of the Khyrim Syiemship (Khasi Kingdom) praying for peace and abundant crops.
cultural_significance: Khasi royal maidens in pure gold and silver crowns and silk jainsems perform slow, dignified steps to the rhythm of Tangmuri pipes and drums.
visitor_tips: Smit is easily reached by shared taxi from Shillong. Silence and decorum should be maintained around the sacred thatch palace (Ling Sad).

name: Brahmaputra River Beach Festival
description: Winter river carnival transforming Guwahati's seasonal sandy river beaches into a vibrant celebration of food, music, and adventure.
cultural_significance: Traditional boat racing, beach volleyball, indigenous Assamese folk sports, paramotoring, sand art sculptures, and sunset folk concerts.
visitor_tips: Walking distance from Fancy Bazar and Umananda ghat. Free entry. Best sunset views across the mighty Brahmaputra.
